metadata.Name: HistoiresMorales
metadata.Description: HistoiresMorales is a French dataset for assessing moral alignment, derived from the English MoralStories dataset. It consists of 12,000 short narratives describing moral and deviant behaviour in various social situations. The stories were translated and subsequently refined with native speakers to ensure grammatical accuracy and cultural adaptation to the French context.
Provider: Télécom Paris, Institut Polytechnique de Paris
metadata.Paper Title: HistoiresMorales: A French Dataset for Assessing Moral Alignment
metadata.Venue Title: Proceedings of the 61st Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
Affiliations: Laboratoire Hubert Curien, UMR CNRS 5516, Saint-Etienne, France

metadata.Abstract: Aligning language models with human values is crucial, especially as they become more integrated into everyday life. nWhile models are often adapted to user preferences, it is equally important to ensure they align with moral norms and behaviours in real-world social situations. nDespite significant progress in languages like English and Chinese, French has seen little attention in this area, leaving a gap in understanding how LLMs handle moral reasoning in this language.nTo address this gap, we introduce ntextsc{HistoiresMorales}, a French dataset derived from textsc{MoralStories}, created through translation and subsequently refined with the assistance of native speakers to guarantee grammatical accuracy and adaptation to the French cultural context. nWe also rely on annotations of the moral values within the dataset to ensure their alignment with French norms.ntextsc{HistoiresMorales} covers a wide range of social situations, including differences in tipping practices, nexpressions of honesty in relationships, and responsibilities toward animals.nTo foster future research, we also conduct preliminary experiments on the alignment of multilingual models on French and English data and the robustness of the alignment.nWe find that while LLMs are generally aligned with human moral norms by default, they can be easily influenced with user-preference optimization for both moral and immoral data.
